question: Consider all European cities that have ever hosted a World Expo (up to and including 2020) according to the Bureau International des Expositions (not Specialized Expos) but are not the capital of their respective country. List the year of the most recent World Expo hosted by each of those cities that are on the Iberian Peninsula.

answer:
According to the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE), considering only **International Registered Exhibitions** (World Expos) up to and including 2020 (and excluding Specialized Expos), the non-capital European cities on the Iberian Peninsula that have hosted such expos are **Barcelona** and **Seville**.

Here are the most recent World Expo years for each:
- **Barcelona, Spain**: 1929 (hosted as an International Registered Exhibition; Madrid is Spain's capital)
- **Seville, Spain**: 1992 (hosted Expo '92; Madrid is Spain's capital)

Note: Lisbon, Portugal, hosted the 1998 expo on oceans, but this was classified as a **Specialized Expo** (International Recognised Exhibition) and is therefore excluded per your criteria.

and **"Specialised Exhibitions"**.*   **1988 Amendment (Current System, effective 1996):** Officially reclassified them to:    *   **"International Registered Exhibitions"** (Commonly called World Expos / formerly Universal).    *   **"International Recognised Exhibitions"** (Commonly called Specialised Expos / formerly Specialised).**Key Differences Between Categories (Current Rules):**| Feature | World Expos (International Registered Exhibitions) | Specialised Expos (International Recognised Exhibitions) || :--- | :--- | :--- || **Theme Focus** | Addresses a **universal challenge** customize pavilions **provided by the Organiser** (rent-free modules). || **Frequency** | Every **five years** (minimum interval established by 1988 Amendment). | Held **between two World Expos** (interval limited to once every 5 years since 1988). || **Participants** | Countries, International Organizations, Cities, Companies, NGOs (All categories). | Primarily Countries and International Organizations (Non-official participants like cities/companies allowed but limited scope). |**Relevance to Historical Verification (Iberian Peninsula Context):***   **Seville 1992:** Categorized under the modern standard as a **World Expo** (Universal/Registered).*   **Zaragoza 2008:** Noted as the **first Specialised Expo** (Recognised) organized under the new 1988 Amendment rules.
